title: Platelet Activation by Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs) in the Göttingen Minipig, including an Evaluation of Glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Ontogeny
authors_year: Jordal, Berridge, et al. (2023)
species_and_system: Göttingen minipig platelet-rich plasma and whole blood in vitro (activation assay + aggregometry), explicitly cross-tabulated against published human PRP/whole-blood and NHP data for the same seven constructs
why_relevant: The single highest-value record found. Table 1 gives complete per-position chemistry for 7 tool ASOs — PS linkage positions marked residue-by-residue with asterisks, 2'MOE sugar positions as uppercase, LNA positions as underlined uppercase — with length and explicit PS load (e.g. ODN2395 22-mer/21 PS; ISIS104838 2'MOE/PS/2'MOE gapmer 20-mer/19 PS; RTR5001 LNA/PS/LNA 14-mer/13 PS), plus isosequential PO and all-PS variants that isolate backbone from sugar chemistry. Table 2 is a purpose-built human/NHP/minipig bridge matrix for those same 7 constructs across in vivo and in vitro platelet endpoints. Mechanism is PS ASO binding to platelet collagen receptor GPVI, stated to mirror human blood findings. CC BY, so tables are directly reusable.

title: A Comparative Study of Porcine and Ovine Derived Defibrotide: Coagulation Profiles, Molecular Characteristics, and DNA Content
authors_year: Clin Appl Thromb Hemost (2026)
species_and_system: Human blood-bank pooled plasma plus individually analysed healthy volunteer donor plasma and citrated human whole blood, spiked at 100 µg/mL
why_relevant: Closes gaps 1 and 4 simultaneously and is the only record found that does so. 19 porcine and 9 ovine defibrotide API batches each assayed by aPTT and thrombin time in human plasma and whole blood, with anti-Xa and anti-IIa amidolytic activities — directly the anti-Xa and contact/common-pathway endpoint set requested. Characterisation is per-batch: DNA content by heparin-red quantification and molecular weight distribution by size-exclusion HPLC (tandem PSK 2000/3000, heparin fraction calibrators 2,000–50,000). Methods state donor plasma was analysed individually and not pooled, so donor-level conditions are recoverable. Caveat the authors disclose: no untreated control samples were included.

title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex
authors_year: Sheehan & Lan, Blood (1998)
species_and_system: Human plasma in vitro coagulation assays plus purified human component systems (thrombin clotting activity, heparin cofactor II)
why_relevant: Foundational human in vitro record for the PS-backbone coagulopathy signal. ISIS 2302 (20-mer PS, anti-ICAM-1) characterised in human plasma and in purified human enzyme systems, locating the dominant effect at the intrinsic tenase (FIXa-FVIIIa) complex, with prothrombin-time and thrombin-time prolongation above ~100 µg/mL and a separate heparin-cofactor-II-mediated component. The abstract itself frames the work as explaining clotting-time prolongation seen in both monkey and human dosing of the same construct, so it anchors a same-construct bridge with PMID 9316823 (human volunteers) and PMID 9361909 (cynomolgus).

title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex by an allosteric mechanism
authors_year: Biochemistry (2001)
species_and_system: Purified human coagulation factors (FIXa, FVIIIa, FX, phospholipid) and human plasma aPTT
why_relevant: The quantitative mechanistic follow-up to the record above, and the best purified-human-factor dataset found. States plainly that PS oligodeoxynucleotides prolong aPTT in human plasma by inhibiting intrinsic tenase activity, then dissects it with ISIS 2302: hyperbolic mixed-type inhibition of FX activation, Vmax(app) decomposition across complex assembly, cofactor stability and protease catalysis, with controls showing no inhibition of FIXa-phospholipid FX activation and no significant effect on FVIII-phospholipid affinity. Gives mechanism-level parameters rather than a single clotting-time shift, which is what distinguishes a reusable in vitro assay row from an observation.

title: Effects of synthetic oligonucleotides on human complement and coagulation
authors_year: Biochem Pharmacol (1997)
species_and_system: Normal human donor plasma and human blood in vitro; hemolytic complement assay
why_relevant: Explicitly constructed as the human in vitro counterpart to the unanticipated monkey findings, which is exactly the bridge framing gap 2 asks for. PS-oligo inhibited normal human blood clotting with concentration-dependent prolongation of clotting times including aPTT, measured alongside prothrombin fragment F1+2 and hemolytic complement in the same donor plasma — giving a coagulation and complement readout on one material, useful for separating contact-pathway activation from complement-driven effects in the dataset.

title: Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation
authors_year: Bioorg Med Chem Lett (1998)
species_and_system: Human plasma in vitro aPTT and complement lysis
why_relevant: The only record found that resolves the aPTT effect by sugar chemistry class within one experiment: synthesised and compared PS-oligodeoxyribonucleotide (DNA) against PS-oligoribonucleotide, 2'-O-methyl-RNA and 2'-5'-RNA analogues for aPTT prolongation and complement lysis inhibition in vitro, concluding PS-DNA prolongs aPTT and inhibits complement lysis more than the PS-RNA analogues. That is a chemistry-resolved structure-activity axis for coagulopathy, directly serving the Phase 2 requirement to locate chemical modifications rather than just name a compound.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety of fesomersen, a novel antisense inhibitor of factor XI, in healthy Chinese, Japanese, and Caucasian volunteers
authors_year: Clin Transl Sci (2024)
species_and_system: Healthy human volunteers (three clinical studies, three ethnic groups), subcutaneous dosing, FXI activity and clotting-time PD
why_relevant: Open-access (CC BY-NC) human PK/PD/safety dataset for a GalNAc-conjugated FXI ASO across three ethnic cohorts, which lets FXI-lowering and the resulting clotting-time change be read against exposure rather than dose alone. Three studies reported in one paper, so it is efficient to ingest, and the ethnic-cohort structure supports covariate work that single-cohort trial reports cannot. Full text is retrievable, so PD tables and any sequence/chemistry statement are inspectable without a paywall route.

title: Factor XI antisense oligonucleotide for prevention of venous thrombosis
authors_year: Büller et al., N Engl J Med (2015)
species_and_system: 300 human patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, randomised open-label FXI-ASO (ISIS 416858) vs enoxaparin
why_relevant: The pivotal human interventional dataset for a second-generation 2'-MOE PS antisense agent whose on-target effect is itself a coagulopathy: FXI level reduction with corresponding aPTT prolongation, read against adjudicated VTE and bleeding endpoints in 300 participants. Free full text is available as a PMC author manuscript, so the endpoint tables are reachable without a subscription. Pairs with PMID 22246038 below on the identical construct.

title: Antisense inhibition of coagulation factor XI prolongs APTT without increased bleeding risk in cynomolgus monkeys
authors_year: Younis et al., Blood (2012)
species_and_system: Cynomolgus monkey, up to 13 weeks subcutaneous dosing; liver FXI mRNA, plasma FXI activity, APTT, bleeding models
why_relevant: Supplies the animal half of a genuine same-construct human-to-animal bridge: ISIS 416858 is the identical 2'-MOE antisense inhibitor of FXI dosed in the NEJM trial above. Reports a dose-dependent FXI reduction (liver mRNA and plasma activity) with concomitant APTT increase across 4–40 mg/kg/week, plus explicit bleeding-risk assessment at 20 and 40 mg/kg/week. Because both the exposure-response and the APTT endpoint are measured in the same units as the human study, the two can be aligned rather than merely compared qualitatively — which is the specific operation gap 2 requires.

title: Fitusiran prophylaxis in people with severe haemophilia A or haemophilia B without inhibitors (ATLAS-A/B): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
authors_year: Srivastava et al., Lancet Haematol (2023)
species_and_system: Human, 45 sites in 17 countries, males aged 12+ with severe haemophilia A or B without inhibitors, randomised 2:1 to 80 mg monthly subcutaneous fitusiran vs on-demand clotting factor concentrates, 9 months
why_relevant: This is named acquisition target 5 and I confirmed the exact primary publication: PubMed's NCT03417245 secondary-source index resolves to this record and no other trial report. Fitusiran is an antithrombin-targeting siRNA whose mechanism is deliberate induced hypercoagulability, so its safety appendix is the counterpart case to the aPTT-prolonging ASOs — the thrombotic-event and antithrombin-level data are the coagulopathy endpoint. Access caveat: no PMC record and not in Europe PMC, so the full text and safety appendix are behind Lancet Haematol; I found no legal open copy via PMC or EPMC.

title: First-in-human experience of an antidote-controlled anticoagulant using RNA aptamer technology: a phase 1a pharmacodynamic evaluation of a drug-antidote pair for the controlled regulation of factor IXa activity
authors_year: Dyke et al., Circulation (2006)
species_and_system: Healthy human volunteers, phase 1a; REG1 system (RB006 modified-RNA aptamer drug, RB007 complementary oligonucleotide antidote)
why_relevant: Covers the pegnivacogin/REG1 branch of the named vocabulary with first-in-human dose-response clotting-time data, and is mechanistically distinct from every other record here: anticoagulation is the intended pharmacology via FIXa binding, and it is actively reversible by a complementary oligonucleotide. That reversal arm is unusually informative for the dataset because it gives a within-subject on/off control on an oligonucleotide-driven clotting-time change. Pairs with PMID 18284597 (randomised repeat-dose PD study of the same pair) for a dose-ranging extension.

title: Pharmacokinetic properties of ISIS 2302, an antisense inhibitor of intercellular adhesion molecule-1, in healthy male volunteers (rising-dose, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial)
authors_year: Glover et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther (1997)
species_and_system: Healthy male human volunteers, single and multiple IV infusions, 0.06–2.00 mg/kg over 2 h
why_relevant: Completes a same-construct triangle that no other compound in this search offers: ISIS 2302 measured in human volunteers here, in human plasma and purified human factors in PMIDs 9716589 and 11305914, and in cynomolgus monkeys in PMID 9361909. Reports brief dose-related aPTT increases timed to Cmax with Cmax linearly related to dose, plus clinically insignificant C3a rises at higher repeated doses while C5a, blood pressure and pulse were unaffected — giving a concentration-anchored human in vivo aPTT point that can be regressed against the in vitro inhibition constants from the same molecule.

title: A Comparative Study of Porcine and Ovine Derived Defibrotide: Coagulation Profiles, Molecular Characteristics, and DNA Content
authors_year: Clin Appl Thromb Hemost, 2026
species_and_system: HUMAN. Citrated blood-bank plasma (Loyola University Medical Center Blood Bank) plus citrated whole blood from multiple healthy adult volunteers aged 18-40, processed and analysed individually, NOT pooled across donors. Verified by reading the OA full text, not the abstract (the abstract says only 'pooled plasma').
why_relevant: The single best dual-gap record found in this resource. Closes gap 1 and gap 4 simultaneously for an oligonucleotide drug. Human plasma and human whole blood spiked at 100 ug/mL with 28 separate API batches (19 porcine, 9 ovine) of defibrotide, read out by aPTT (Instrumentation Laboratory ACL 300), thrombin time (Stago ST4), and amidolytic anti-Xa and anti-IIa. Reported result is a NEGATIVE aPTT finding (no anticoagulant effect in aPTT for either source) with mild comparable effect in TT - a genuine human in vitro negative control point, which a coagulopathy dataset needs as much as positives. Separately provides batch-level tested-material characterisation: size-exclusion chromatography molecular weight (ovine 16.8 +/- 0.24 kDa vs porcine 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa) and DNA content by heparin red method (75.78 vs 79 ug per 10 ug API). Caveat for dataset entry: defibrotide is a polydisperse DNA-derived polyelectrolyte, so there is no single definable sequence - record it as a mixture with MW distribution rather than forcing a sequence field. Also note the paper states untreated control samples were not included.

title: Sequence-specific 2'-O-methoxyethyl antisense oligonucleotides activate human platelets through glycoprotein VI, triggering formation of platelet-leukocyte aggregates
authors_year: Haematologica, 2022
species_and_system: HUMAN. Human cord-blood-derived megakaryocytes (proplatelet production) and whole blood from healthy human volunteers (surface P-selectin, platelet-leukocyte aggregates); GPVI binding affinity measured directly.
why_relevant: Highest-value gap 1 record for the phosphorothioate platelet/thrombocytopenia axis, and it is explicitly sequence-resolved, which is rare. Five named phosphorothioate ASOs tested side by side: three 2'MOE compounds - ISIS 487660 (no effect on platelet count), ISIS 104838 (associated with clinical phenotype 1 platelet decline), ISIS 501861 (effect unknown) - plus two CpG sequences, ISIS 120704 and ODN 2395. All five bound platelet GPVI with KD ~0.2-1.5 mM; CpG had highest affinity and greatest activation; 487660 showed no detectable platelet effect while 104838 and 501861 drove SYK-dependent platelet-leukocyte aggregate formation. Critically for the Phase 2 criteria, it reports donor-level stratification: donors with higher platelet GPVI levels showed greater ASO-induced activation, which is exactly the kind of human-system variance data the challenge asks for. None of the ASOs inhibited proplatelet production, which localises the mechanism to activation rather than production. Named compound IDs make per-position chemistry recoverable even where this paper does not print the base sequence.

title: The Influence of Plasma Prekallikrein Oligonucleotide Antisense Therapy on Coagulation and Fibrinolysis Assays: A Post-hoc Analysis
authors_year: Fijen, Petersen, Meijers, Bordone, Levi, Cohn; Thromb Haemost, 2022
species_and_system: HUMAN ex vivo. Patient plasma from a phase 2 randomised trial, 22 hereditary angioedema patients, donidalorsen 80 mg (IONIS-PKKRx, prekallikrein-targeted 2'MOE ASO) vs placebo, baseline and 4-month follow-up.
why_relevant: The most complete human coagulation panel found on a clinically dosed antisense oligonucleotide, and it is fully extractable: the Europe PMC record carries no abstract, so this is only visible by reading the CC-BY full text, which I did. Table 1 gives numeric baseline/follow-up/delta values with p-values and reference ranges for silica-based aPTT (reported as remaining within reference values), calibrated automated thrombogram lag time, peak thrombin and ETP, factor XI activity, prothrombin fragment 1+2, thrombin-antithrombin complexes, high-molecular-weight kininogen activity, normalised clot lysis time, D-dimer, plasminogen activity, and plasmin-alpha2-antiplasmin complexes. Median prekallikrein reduction 75% (range 36-94%). Directly addresses the contact-pathway question in gap 1 with a human-system readout, and because prekallikrein deficiency itself prolongs aPTT, the negative aPTT result here is a mechanistically load-bearing data point. Ionis co-authorship (Bordone) means these are sponsor-grade assay data.

title: Assessing single-stranded oligonucleotide drug-induced effects in vitro reveals key risk factors for thrombocytopenia
authors_year: Sewing et al.; PLoS One, 2017
species_and_system: HUMAN. Human platelets in vitro; human haematopoietic cell differentiation culture.
why_relevant: The structure-activity backbone for gap 1: it converts 'phosphorothioates activate platelets' into a quantitative chemistry relationship in a human system. Shows PS-oligonucleotide binding to human platelet GPVI and, newly, to platelet factor 4, with binding and subsequent human platelet activation correlating with oligonucleotide LENGTH and with the NUMBER OF PHOSPHOROTHIOATE LINKAGES in the backbone. Also shows locked nucleic acid (LNA) ribosyl modifications in the wings strongly suppress both GPVI and PF4 binding and markedly reduce platelet activation - i.e. per-position chemistry changes the coagulopathy readout, which is precisely the extrapolation axis the Phase 2 call privileges. Explicitly framed as a prospective in vitro assay battery for deprioritising thrombocytopenia-liable candidates, so the assay conditions are documented for reuse. PS count and length are both encodable as dataset covariates.

title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators
authors_year: Flierl et al.; J Exp Med, 2015
species_and_system: HUMAN platelets (plus animal work in the same paper).
why_relevant: The originating mechanistic paper attributing platelet activation specifically to the PHOSPHOROTHIOATE BACKBONE rather than to sequence or target, across nucleotide-based drug classes. It is the reference that the Haematologica and Sewing human-platelet studies build on, so including it gives the dataset the mechanistic root node for the whole PS-backbone coagulopathy cluster. Open access in PMC with no retrieval barrier. Because it spans human platelets and in vivo animal work within one paper, it is also a candidate partial bridge for gap 2, though the construct matching across species needs checking against the methods before claiming it as one.

title: RNA interference therapy targeting coagulation factor XI: a first-in-human trial of RBD4059 (vortosiran)
authors_year: Gabrielsen et al. (Ribocure/Suzhou Ribo); Blood Advances, 2026
species_and_system: HUMAN. Phase 1 single ascending dose, healthy volunteers, randomised 6+2 active:placebo across four subcutaneous cohorts 50-600 mg, followed to day 169.
why_relevant: HUMAN HALF OF THE CLEANEST HUMAN-TO-ANIMAL BRIDGE I FOUND. Same named construct (RBD4059, GalNAc-conjugated siRNA targeting FXI) measured here in humans and in mice and monkeys in the companion record below, so the two sides are directly comparable - which is exactly what gap 2 asks for and is usually impossible to assemble because sponsors publish preclinical and clinical data under different compound labels. Reports dose-dependent, durable suppression of FXI activity exceeding 90%, with safety and tolerability as primary endpoint to day 169, plus PK/PD modelling supporting 3-6 month dosing. FXI activity is the pharmacodynamic coagulation readout, so this is on-target coagulation modulation rather than off-target coagulopathy - worth encoding with that distinction explicit, since conflating intended FXI knockdown with phosphorothioate contact-pathway toxicity would corrupt the dataset.

title: Inhibition of Factor XI Using RBD4059: A Novel GalNAc-siRNA With Potent and Durable Antithrombotic Effects
authors_year: JACC Basic Transl Sci, 2025
species_and_system: ANIMAL. Mice and cynomolgus monkeys (FXI inhibition, duration), mouse thrombosis models, mouse tail bleeding model.
why_relevant: ANIMAL HALF OF THE RBD4059/VORTOSIRAN BRIDGE. Pair this with PMC13083634 above and the dataset gains a matched same-construct human/animal comparison for a GalNAc-siRNA acting on the coagulation cascade: potent durable FXI inhibition in both mice and monkeys, antithrombotic efficacy in mouse thrombosis models, and no prolonged bleeding in the mouse tail bleed assay, against >90% FXI suppression and no safety signal in human healthy volunteers. That lets the extrapolation the Phase 2 call asks for (animal to human system) be computed rather than asserted. Both halves are open access with no retrieval barrier.

title: Chemistry, structure and function of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics
authors_year: Egli & Manoharan; Nucleic Acids Research, 2023
species_and_system: Not applicable - chemistry reference work covering 18 approved nucleic acid therapeutics.
why_relevant: Best single instrument found in this resource for gap 3, where only 14 of 38 human-dosed compounds currently have a printed sequence and 11 have position-level chemistry. Systematic treatment of the chemistry of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics with per-modification structural detail across phosphorothioate, 2'-F-RNA, 2'-O-methyl RNA, 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl)-RNA (MOE) and phosphorodiamidate morpholino chemistries. Disease coverage explicitly includes homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (mipomersen), hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (inotersen) and familial chylomicronemia syndrome (volanesorsen) - the three approved compounds that carry the heaviest coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia signal in this dataset. Open access in PMC. Use it to populate position-level chemistry for approved compounds; it will NOT cover the discontinued or investigational ISIS-numbered compounds, which still need sponsor filings or patent literature.

title: Assessment of Platelet Aggregation and Thrombin Generation in Patients with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome Treated with Volanesorsen: A Cross-Sectional Study
authors_year: Biomedicines, 2024
species_and_system: HUMAN ex vivo. 4 FCS patients on volanesorsen plus 4 matched healthy controls; samples processed by calibrated automated thrombogram (CAT, PPP-reagent LOW) and turbidimetric platelet aggregation against multiple agonists.
why_relevant: Rare functional human coagulation phenotyping on a clinically dosed ASO, as opposed to platelet counts alone. Gives numeric thrombin generation parameters for patients and controls (LagTime, ttPeak, StartTail, Velocity Index, ETP, peak thrombin - e.g. ETP 599.80 +/- 73.47 in patients vs 900.2 +/- 210.99 in controls) alongside platelet count change from baseline of 30% at week 12 and 34% at week 36. Finding is that thrombin generation and aggregation stayed within range with no significant case-control difference despite the platelet count drop, which is a mechanistically important dissociation: volanesorsen lowers platelet NUMBER without a detectable global haemostatic functional deficit. Must be entered with n=4 and the cross-sectional design on its face - it is a small-n study and its value is the assay depth and the dissociation finding, not statistical weight. Note Europe PMC also holds a preprint of the same work (10.20944/preprints202407.0557.v1); dedupe against the journal version.

title: The Effects of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Containing Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelets in Human Clinical Trials
authors_year: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2017
species_and_system: HUMAN. Ionis integrated safety database (ISDB): over 2,600 human subjects across 16 different 2'MOE ASOs, placebo-controlled and open-label, doses to 624 mg/week, durations to 4.6 years.
why_relevant: The denominator record for the 2'MOE platelet signal, and it is sequence-discriminating at the class level, which matters for the dataset's extrapolation claims. Establishes there is no class-generic 2'MOE effect on platelet number, no confirmed counts below 50 K/uL, and only 7 of 2,638 subjects (0.3%) with a confirmed post-baseline count between 100 and 50 K/uL - but that 3 of 16 2'MOE ASOs had >10% incidence of platelet decreases >30% from baseline, i.e. the liability is sequence-specific rather than chemistry-generic. That conclusion is the clinical counterpart to the in vitro sequence-specificity in PMC8804562 and PMC5673186, so the three together let the dataset link a human in vitro assay result to a human trial outcome. Also reports no evidence of altered platelet FUNCTION, including from the factor XI ASO trials. Does not print sequences; compounds are referenced at class level.

identifier: PMID 31390500 / DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1715944 (APPROACH, volanesorsen, sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS6)
title: Volanesorsen and Triglyceride Levels in Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome
authors_year: Witztum et al.; N Engl J Med, 2019
species_and_system: HUMAN. APPROACH randomised placebo-controlled phase 3, 33 volanesorsen vs 33 placebo.
why_relevant: NAMED ACQUISITION TARGET FROM GAP 5, PARTIALLY CLOSED BY A LEGAL OPEN ROUTE. The NEJM version is subscription-only and has no PMC record, but Europe PMC's fullTextUrlList surfaced an author/institutional repository copy at Amsterdam UMC Pure flagged 'Open access'. I fetched it and confirmed HTTP 200, a real 414 KB PDF, and extracted the adverse event table from it: platelet count decreased 11/33 (33%) volanesorsen vs 1/33 (3%) placebo; petechiae 4 (12%) vs 0; epistaxis 5 (15%) vs 0; injection-site reaction 20 (61%) vs 0. These are directly enterable coagulopathy rows for a clinically dosed ASO. IMPORTANT LIMITATION, verified by text scan of the retrieved PDF: it contains the main article only. Zero matches for 'supplementary appendix', 'sequence', 'purity' or 'aPTT'. So the SUPPLEMENTARY APPENDIX half of this gap-5 target remains unclosed, and the per-patient platelet time course, sequence and purity data presumably in it are still outstanding. Try the FDA/EMA review documents or the sponsor protocol next, not Europe PMC.

identifier: PMID 9716589 / DOI 10.1182/blood.v92.5.1617 (with companion PMID 11305914, DOI 10.1021/bi002396x, Biochemistry 2001)
title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex (1998); companion: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex by an allosteric mechanism (2001)
authors_year: Sheehan & Lan, Blood 1998; Sheehan & Phan, Biochemistry 2001
species_and_system: PURIFIED HUMAN COAGULATION FACTORS. Intrinsic tenase complex (factor VIIIa/factor IXa activation of factor X) in a reconstituted purified system.
why_relevant: The mechanistic anchor for phosphorothioate aPTT prolongation at the purified-human-factor level, which is the most reductionist tier of gap 1 and the tier the dataset most lacks. Together the pair establishes that PS oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex and do so by an ALLOSTERIC mechanism, not simple polyanionic surface sequestration - that distinction determines whether aPTT prolongation should be modelled as concentration-linear nonspecific polyanion effect or as a saturable binding event, and it changes how the dataset should extrapolate between assay formats. Found alongside two further foundational closed-access records from the same era: 'Inhibition of coagulation by a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide' (PMID 9361909, Antisense Nucleic Acid Drug Dev 1997) and Henry et al. 'Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation' (PMID 9873494, Bioorg Med Chem Lett 1998). ACCESS: Europe PMC advertises the Blood 1998 full text as 'Free after 12 months' at the legacy bloodjournal.org URL, but I followed the DOI and ashpublications.org returned HTTP 403 - see the barrier field. Abstract is free; full text

title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators
authors_year: Flierl U, Nero TL, Lim B, et al. 2015, J Exp Med 212(2):129
species_and_system: HUMAN washed platelets and whole blood in vitro (healthy donors); platelets from GPVI function-deficient PATIENTS ex vivo; plus mouse in vivo thrombus formation
why_relevant: Highest-value gap-1 record found. Direct PS-backbone-dependent human platelet activation, signalling, ROS, adhesion, spreading, aggregation and in vitro thrombus formation, with GPVI identified as the receptor. The GPVI-deficient patient platelets give a human mechanistic negative control, and the paired mouse in vivo work makes it a bridge record as well. JEM supplementary carries the oligonucleotide panel.

title: Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides Inhibit the Intrinsic Tenase Complex
authors_year: Sheehan JP, Lan HC 1998, Blood 92(5):1617
species_and_system: HUMAN plasma in vitro coagulation assays + purified HUMAN enzyme systems (thrombin, heparin cofactor II, intrinsic tenase); explicitly anchored to prior monkey AND human in vivo clotting-time prolongation
why_relevant: Canonical gap-1 source. A single defined 20-mer PS ASO (ISIS 2302, anti-ICAM-1) titrated in human plasma with PT, thrombin time and aPTT endpoints, then dissected in purified human component assays. Because the abstract frames the in vitro work against both monkey and human dosing data, it doubles as a human-to-animal bridge for ISIS 2302. Concentration-response in ug/mL is extractable.

title: Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides Inhibit the Intrinsic Tenase Complex by an Allosteric Mechanism
authors_year: Sheehan JP, Phan TM 2001, Biochemistry 40(16):4980
species_and_system: HUMAN plasma aPTT + purified human factor IXa / factor VIIIa / factor X kinetics
why_relevant: Mechanistic follow-up to the 1998 Blood paper, same construct ISIS 2302. States directly that PS ODNs prolong aPTT in human plasma by inhibiting intrinsic tenase (FIXa-FVIIIa), and resolves it as hyperbolic mixed-type inhibition with complex-assembly, cofactor-stability and catalysis sub-experiments. This is the quantitative human mechanism row behind the aPTT signal that recurs across the whole PS class.

title: Integrated Safety Assessment of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides in NonHuman Primates and Healthy Human Volunteers
authors_year: Crooke ST, Baker BF, Kwoh TJ, et al. 2016, Mol Ther 24(10):1771
species_and_system: Macaque (cynomolgus) controlled dose-ranging AND healthy HUMAN volunteer dose-ranging, 12 unique 2'-MOE chimeric ASOs
why_relevant: The strongest gap-2 record in this resource: twelve distinct 2'-MOE constructs measured under matched dose-ranging designs in both NHP and healthy humans, with standardised haematology, complement and platelet panels. Explicitly quantifies where the animal data over-predicts human risk (complement activation, platelet effects) and where NHP correctly predicted safe human doses. This is exactly the in vitro/animal-to-human extrapolation Phase 2 asks for, at class rather than single-compound level.

title: Factor XI Antisense Oligonucleotide for Prevention of Venous Thrombosis
authors_year: Buller HR, Bethune C, Bhanot S, et al. 2014, N Engl J Med 372(3):232
species_and_system: HUMAN interventional trial, n=300 total knee arthroplasty patients, FXI-ASO (ISIS 416858 / IONIS-FXIRx) 200 mg and 300 mg vs enoxaparin 40 mg
why_relevant: Human trial endpoint record for the FXI ASO with coagulopathy as the on-target pharmacology: FXI activity reduction, aPTT prolongation, venographic VTE incidence and a prespecified major/clinically-relevant bleeding safety outcome. Free via PMC and via the Amsterdam UMC Pure repository, so the safety tables are retrievable. Pairs one-to-one with the Younis monkey record below on the identical construct.
already_in_our_sources: UNKNOWN - likely already present, canonical FXI-ASO trial primary publication

title: Antisense inhibition of coagulation factor XI prolongs APTT without increased bleeding risk in cynomolgus monkeys
authors_year: Younis HS, Crosby JR, Huh JI, et al. 2012, Blood 119(10):2401
species_and_system: Cynomolgus monkey, ISIS 416858 (2'-MOE ASO), 4/8/12/20/40 mg/kg/wk SC up to 13 weeks
why_relevant: The animal half of the cleanest human-to-animal bridge available: SAME construct (ISIS 416858) as the Buller trial, SAME endpoints (plasma FXI activity, aPTT, PT, platelets, provoked bleeding after tail amputation and gum/skin laceration). Gives dose-dependent FXI knockdown versus aPTT change (80% FXI reduction to 33% aPTT increase) directly comparable with the human trial numbers. Named chemistry (2'-MOE) and free publisher PDF.

title: IONIS-PKK Rx, a Novel Antisense Inhibitor of Prekallikrein and Bradykinin Production
authors_year: 2019, Nucleic Acid Therapeutics 29(2):82
species_and_system: Transgenic mice + cynomolgus monkeys + healthy HUMAN volunteers; human plasma prekallikrein protein and plasma bradykinin-generation capacity
why_relevant: Contact-pathway record covering the exact gap-1 vocabulary (prekallikrein) and the gap-2 bridge in one paper: one named 2'-MOE chimeric ASO (the donidalorsen predecessor) measured as hepatic PKK mRNA and plasma PKK in mice, plasma PKK in monkeys, and plasma PKK plus ex vivo bradykinin-generation capacity in healthy humans. Nucleic Acid Therapeutics is the journal family that routinely prints full sequence and per-position chemistry, so this is also a gap-3 candidate. Free via PMC.

title: Platelet Activation by Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs) in the Gottingen Minipig, including an Evaluation of Glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Ontogeny
authors_year: Valenzuela A, Ayuso M, Buyssens LA, et al. 2023, Pharmaceutics 15(4):1112
species_and_system: Gottingen minipig platelets in vitro (adult and juvenile) with explicit comparison against HUMAN platelet data; multiple ASO sequences and modification patterns
why_relevant: Best gap-3 plus gap-2 combination in this resource: tests a panel of several ASO sequences and chemical modification patterns in in vitro platelet activation and aggregometry, states the adult-minipig results are closely comparable with human data, and confirms PS ASO binding to the collagen receptor GPVI. Gold OA (CC-BY) with a sequence/modification table and PF4/GPVI abundance quantitation, so per-position chemistry should be extractable rather than inferred.

title: Direct factor IXa inhibition with the RNA-aptamer pegnivacogin reduces platelet reactivity in vitro and residual platelet aggregation in patients with acute coronary syndromes
authors_year: Staudacher DL, Putz V, Heger LA, et al. 2017, Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
species_and_system: HUMAN whole blood from healthy volunteers incubated in vitro; plus ex vivo platelet aggregometry on blood from ACS patients dosed in the RADAR trial
why_relevant: One of very few records pairing a human in vitro oligonucleotide blood assay with ex vivo samples from dosed human participants on the same readout. Covers a chemistry class the dataset needs beyond PS gapmers (PEGylated RNA aptamer, FIXa-directed, with the anivamersen reversal agent) and gives platelet reactivity rather than only clotting times. Donor-level whole-blood conditions are reported.

title: Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Mipomersen in Patients with Severe Hypercholesterolemia Receiving Maximally Tolerated Lipid-Lowering Therapy
authors_year: McGowan MP, Tardif JC, Ceska R, et al. 2012, PLoS ONE 7(11):e49006
species_and_system: HUMAN interventional trial, n=58 (mipomersen 200 mg weekly SC n=39 vs placebo n=19), 26 weeks
why_relevant: Named acquisition target: this is the ISIS 301012-CS12 mipomersen trial, and unlike the sibling mipomersen trials it is gold open access in PLoS ONE with PMC deposit, so the individual safety tables and supporting information files are directly retrievable rather than paywalled. Closes the CS12 leg of the gap-5 mipomersen request.
already_in_our_sources: UNKNOWN - likely already present, mipomersen CS12 primary publication

title: Volanesorsen and Triglyceride Levels in Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (APPROACH)
authors_year: Witztum JL, Gaudet D, Freedman SD, et al. 2019, N Engl J Med 381(6):531
species_and_system: HUMAN interventional trial, n=66 FCS patients, volanesorsen vs placebo, 52 weeks
why_relevant: Named acquisition target (APPROACH, sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS6). OpenAlex resolves a LEGAL green open copy in the Amsterdam UMC Pure institutional repository even though the NEJM version is closed, which is the access route the gap list was missing. Volanesorsen is the key platelet-count/thrombocytopenia signal compound in the dataset, so the 52-week safety reporting matters directly to the coagulopathy endpoint.
already_in_our_sources: UNKNOWN - likely already present, APPROACH primary publication

title: Impurities in Oligonucleotide Drug Substances and Drug Products
authors_year: Capaldi DC, Teasdale A, Henry SP, et al. 2017, Nucleic Acid Therapeutics 27(6):309
species_and_system: Not a biological study: analytical chemistry and regulatory white paper on oligonucleotide drug substance and drug product
why_relevant: The only gap-4 record this resource surfaced. Tenth in the therapeutic-oligonucleotide white paper series, written by Ionis and industry analytical leads; proposes reporting, identification and qualification thresholds for product-related impurities and argues for platform impurity qualification. This is the reference frame for scoring and normalising the dataset's purity-and-characterisation column, rather than a per-compound purity value. No open route found via OpenAlex (no OA location, no PMC deposit).

title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex
authors_year: Sheehan JP, Lan HC — Blood, 1998
species_and_system: Purified human coagulation factors (human FVIIIa/FIXa intrinsic tenase complex) plus human plasma clotting assays
why_relevant: Highest-value gap-1 record surfaced. Mechanistic inhibition of a purified HUMAN factor complex by phosphorothioate oligonucleotides, with reported length- and backbone-dependence — exactly the in-vitro-human-system evidence Phase 2 privileges, and it supplies a mechanism for the aPTT prolongation our dataset currently records only as a clinical observation. Not previously reachable from our PubMed-centric queries because it is indexed under an old Blood locator DOI.

title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex by an allosteric mechanism
authors_year: Sheehan JP et al. — Biochemistry, 2001
species_and_system: Purified human FVIIIa/FIXa (intrinsic tenase), human factor X activation kinetics
why_relevant: The follow-up mechanism paper to the record above, in the same purified human system. Together they give a dose/structure-resolved human in vitro anticoagulant mechanism for PS backbones rather than a single endpoint value — the 'extrapolate between human in vitro and animal data' capability Phase 2 asks for.

title: Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation
authors_year: Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry Letters, 1998
species_and_system: Human serum / human plasma in vitro
why_relevant: Compares phosphorothioate DEOXY versus RIBO oligonucleotides head-to-head on human coagulation and human complement in the same assays. This is a chemistry-resolved structure-activity record in a human system — it is the kind of row that lets the dataset attribute coagulopathy signal to backbone/sugar chemistry rather than to a single named drug.

title: Inhibition of Coagulation by a Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotide
authors_year: Antisense & Nucleic Acid Drug Development, 1997
species_and_system: Human plasma clotting assays in vitro
why_relevant: The foundational human in vitro PS-oligo anticoagulation paper and the seed whose Semantic Scholar citation graph produced most of this list. Worth acquiring in its own right for the human plasma clotting-time concentration-response, and worth keeping as the graph anchor for future sweeps.

title: The Effects of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Containing Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelets in Human Clinical Trials
authors_year: Crooke ST, Baker BF, Witztum JL et al. — Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2017
species_and_system: Human — pooled participant-level platelet data across multiple 2'-MOE ASO clinical trial programmes
why_relevant: Open access, and it is a cross-programme pooled human platelet dataset rather than a single trial. For a dataset with 38 clinically dosed compounds this is a multi-compound human endpoint source with shared chemistry class, and it is the human half of the deliberate human/NHP pair below.

title: Assessment of the Effects of 2'-Methoxyethyl Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelet Count in Cynomolgus Nonhuman Primates
authors_year: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2017
species_and_system: Cynomolgus macaque — platelet count across 2'-MOE ASOs, same chemistry class as the human pooled analysis
why_relevant: Published as the companion to PMID 28145801 by the same group in the same journal and year, covering the same 2'-MOE chemistry class on the same endpoint. The pair is a ready-made human-to-animal bridge on a coagulopathy-adjacent endpoint (platelet count), which is precisely the extrapolation structure Phase 2 says it is particularly interested in.

title: Mechanism of Alternative Complement Pathway Dysregulation by a Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotide in Monkey and Human Serum
authors_year: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2014
species_and_system: Monkey serum AND human serum — the same single phosphorothioate construct in both
why_relevant: A true gap-2 record: one named construct assayed in both a human system and an animal system within one paper, so species sensitivity can be quantified rather than assumed. Endpoint is alternative-pathway complement rather than clotting, so it is a bridge calibration record for PS backbone plasma-protein dysregulation, not a direct coagulopathy row — flag it as adjacent when ingesting.

title: Potent reduction of plasma lipoprotein(a) with an antisense oligonucleotide in human subjects does not affect ex vivo fibrinolysis
authors_year: Journal of Lipid Research, 2019
species_and_system: Human — ex vivo fibrinolysis / clot lysis on plasma from participants dosed with an APO(a) ASO
why_relevant: Open access full text, and an unusual and valuable design: ex vivo human haemostasis assays run on plasma drawn from humans actually receiving the oligonucleotide. That makes it simultaneously a human ex vivo assay row and an in-vivo-anchored one, and it reports a negative/no-effect result, which the dataset needs for balance against the aPTT-positive records.

title: Fitusiran prophylaxis in people with severe haemophilia A or haemophilia B without inhibitors (ATLAS-A/B): a multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial
authors_year: Srivastava A et al. — Lancet Haematology, 2023
species_and_system: Human interventional trial (NCT03417245) — antithrombin-lowering siRNA, thrombotic events and AT activity
why_relevant: NAMED ACQUISITION TARGET #5 located, with a legal open route: Semantic Scholar resolves an author accepted manuscript in the University of Southampton institutional repository (eprints 477603) even though the Lancet Haematology version is paywalled. Note the repository filename refers to ATLAS-INH, so verify on download which ATLAS arm the deposited manuscript actually is before citing it as the ATLAS-A/B primary publication. The safety appendix is a separate supplementary file and was NOT reachable through this resource.

title: Volanesorsen and Triglyceride Levels in Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (APPROACH)
authors_year: Witztum JL et al. — New England Journal of Medicine, 2019
species_and_system: Human interventional trial — volanesorsen phase 3 APPROACH (sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS6), platelet count decline
why_relevant: NAMED ACQUISITION TARGET #5 located with a legal open route: an author accepted manuscript in the Amsterdam UMC Pure repository, bypassing the NEJM paywall. This is the primary publication whose platelet-count and thrombocytopenia tables the dataset needs. The NEJM supplementary appendix itself is a separate file not indexed by this resource — the repository copy may or may not carry it, so check on download.

title: Factor XI Antisense Oligonucleotide for Prevention of Venous Thrombosis
authors_year: Büller HR et al. — New England Journal of Medicine, 2014
species_and_system: Human interventional trial — FXI-ASO (ISIS 416858 / IONIS-FXIRx), aPTT and bleeding endpoints
why_relevant: Already present in the register, listed here only because it is the human anchor of the bridge pair with the primate paper below — Semantic Scholar's citation graph is what made that pairing explicit. No new rows expected from the paper itself.

title: Antithrombotic Effect of Antisense Factor XI Oligonucleotide Treatment in Primates
authors_year: Crosby JR, Marzec U, Revenko AS et al. — ATVB, 2013
species_and_system: Baboon/non-human primate — FXI ASO, aPTT prolongation and thrombus formation
why_relevant: Open access, and the animal arm matching the FXI-ASO human trial above on the same construct and the same aPTT endpoint. Gives the dataset a same-construct human/primate aPTT comparison, which is the cleanest bridge available for the FXI antisense class.

title: From Bench to Bedside and Back: Improving the Safety of GalNAc-siRNA Conjugates Using GNA-Destabilized Seed-Pairing
authors_year: Janas et al. (Alnylam), 2022; GEO release 2022-06-08
species_and_system: Homo sapiens (HepG2.2.15 hepatoma cells) AND Rattus norvegicus (primary rat hepatocytes, PRH; plus Sprague Dawley male rat liver in vivo) — confirmed from the SOFT family file
why_relevant: The single best human-to-animal bridge GEO offers for this dataset: the same GalNAc-siRNA constructs, including the clinically dosed ALN-HBV and its ESC+/GNA redesign, are profiled in a human hepatic system, in primary rat hepatocytes and in rat liver in vivo, explicitly to connect a rodent toxicity signal back to an ALT elevation observed in human healthy volunteers. Per-position chemistry (GNA position, ESC+ pattern) and full sense/antisense sequences are in the open-access NAR supplementary. The toxicity endpoint is hepatotoxicity/ALT, not coagulopathy, so it extends the dataset's chemistry and bridge coverage, not its coagulation rows.

title: ClinASO: a guideline for rapid drug discovery of gapmer antisense oligonucleotides
authors_year: unpublished, GEO release 2025-11-03; no PMID yet
species_and_system: Homo sapiens AND Mus musculus, 12 samples; integrated gapmer ASO design platform, MASLD/liver context
why_relevant: Dual-taxon gapmer ASO series in a hepatic indication — a same-construct human/mouse pairing of exactly the shape gap 2 asks for, from a design platform that should carry systematic per-construct chemistry. Unpublished, so sequence tables are not yet verifiable; worth a direct metadata pull before relying on it.

title: Tuning siRNA Specificity through Seed Region Incorporation of Deoxyribonucleotide Stereoisomers
authors_year: unpublished, GEO release 2026-02-01; no PMID yet
species_and_system: Homo sapiens AND Mus musculus, 104 samples; mouse liver in vivo plus human cultured cells; siRNAs against Ttr, ACTN1, MARC1
why_relevant: Metadata records position-level chemistry per construct directly in GEO: treatment labels Ttr-parent, Ttr-aLd-A7, Ttr-dx-G6, Marc1-dx-G6/G7, Marc1-aLd-G6/G7 encode the exact seed position (6 or 7) and the stereoisomer installed (beta-D-2'-deoxyxylo vs alpha-L-2'-deoxyribo), with doses 0.4/2/10/30/100 mg/kg and batch IDs. TTR is the inotersen/eplontersen target. Human and mouse arms share constructs, so it serves gaps 2 and 3 at once.

title: A therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide encompassing 2'-O-methoxyethyl modification triggers unique perturbation of the transcriptome
authors_year: 2026; GEO release 2026-01-06
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — GM03813 SMA patient skin fibroblasts, 20 samples, 6 uM ASO by nucleofection, RNA at 24 h
why_relevant: Three ASOs against the identical target site (ISS-N1 in SMN2 intron 7, the nusinersen site) differing only in chemistry: PS backbone with 2'-O-methyl, PS backbone with 2'-MOE, and phosphorodiamidate morpholino. Chemistry class is stated per arm in GEO's own overall_design. This is a clean chemistry-controlled human in vitro comparison for a clinically dosed oligo scaffold (nusinersen is 2'-MOE/PS throughout), useful for gap 3 attribution of effects to backbone vs 2'-sugar. No coagulation readout.

title: To scramble or not: steric blocking 2'-MOE/PS control antisense oligonucleotides across cellular models
authors_year: 2026; GEO release 2026-09-17
species_and_system: Homo sapiens (HEK293T, HeLa, SH-SY5Y) plus mouse NIH/3T3; 84 samples; 19 control ASOs (cASO1-cASO19) at 100 nM with TransIT-X2, 48 h
why_relevant: A systematic tolerability screen of 19 well-characterised 2'-MOE/PS control ASOs across human cell models — directly on-point for Phase 2's preference for human in vitro systems and for backbone-attributable (as opposed to target-attributable) effects. Caveat verified from the series_matrix header: GEO stores only the cASO1-19 labels and the transfection protocol, not the sequences; the sequence table is in the paper, so the record needs the publication to satisfy the sequence requirement.

title: Gene expression analysis in liver collected from mice administered non-toxic, toxic, or severely toxic LNA sequences
authors_year: Burdick et al., 2014; GEO release 2014-01-08
species_and_system: Mus musculus (CD-1 male), 56 samples, liver; LNA gapmers NTS-1 (non-toxic), TS-2 (toxic), HTS-3 (severely toxic) at 25 mg/kg SC, 8/16/72 h single dose and 2-week repeat
why_relevant: A sequence-resolved toxicity ladder: three named LNA gapmer sequences explicitly graded non-toxic / toxic / severely toxic with full dosing protocol in the GEO metadata (HTS-3 animals died or were moribund by day 3). Valuable as a sequence-attributable toxicity anchor for gap 3, but animal-only and hepatotoxicity-only, so it cannot serve as a coagulation row or a human bridge.

title: Hepatic gene expression changes following antisense oligonucleotide-based inhibition of miR-29a
authors_year: 2012; GEO release 2012-08-22
species_and_system: Mus musculus (BALB/c female), 8 samples, liver; 20 mg/kg single IP dose
why_relevant: Included as a method finding rather than for its biology: the GEO record itself prints the full ASO sequence (5'-TAACCGATTTCAGATGGTGCTA-3') and its scrambled control (5'-TCATTGGCATGTACCATGCAGCT-3') together with the complete modification scheme (2'-MOE, 2'-F, 2'-alpha-F units on a phosphorothioate backbone, Regulus Therapeutics). It demonstrates that GEO sample metadata is itself a harvestable source of sequence-plus-per-position-chemistry for gap 3 and justifies a bulk SOFT-file sweep of the 304 phosphorothioate and 1,481 gapmer hits for similar printed sequences.

title: Discovery of Long-Acting APOC3 siRNA for Treating Patients with Hypertriglyceridemia
authors_year: 2025; GEO release 2025-09-25
species_and_system: Homo sapiens, 52 samples; GalNAc-conjugated siRNA structure-activity series in human hepatocyte systems
why_relevant: A systematic GalNAc-siRNA SAR series against APOC3 in a human hepatic system — the same target as volanesorsen and olezarsen, two of the dataset's coagulopathy-relevant compounds (volanesorsen's thrombocytopenia signal is the reason APOC3 chemistry matters here). A chemistry-comparison series at that target supports gap 3 chemistry annotation for the APOC3 compound family. No coagulation endpoint.

title: Selection of well-tolerated GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs by screening for RNAi-mediated off-target effects in rodent toxicity studies
authors_year: Janas et al., 2018; GEO release 2018-01-11
species_and_system: Rattus norvegicus, 36 samples; GalNAc-siRNAs at pharmacologically exaggerated doses
why_relevant: The predecessor of GSE184929 and the reference description of the GalNAc-siRNA candidate-selection tox screen whose rat hepatotoxicity gate decides which constructs reach human dosing. Useful for provenance of the chemistry series rather than as an independent data source; rat-only, hepatotoxicity-only, no human arm and no coagulation measurement.

title: RNA Sequencing reveals transcriptome profiling of HUVECs in response to NETs +/- defibrotide
authors_year: 2021; GEO release 2021-10-13
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells, 9 samples; vehicle vs neutrophil extracellular traps vs NETs + defibrotide
why_relevant: The closest GEO comes to a human oligonucleotide-plus-thrombosis record: defibrotide (on the dataset's named vocabulary) applied to human endothelial cells under a NET-driven prothrombotic stimulus, with 229 differentially expressed genes versus NETs alone. Two hard caveats: the readout is transcriptomic, with no aPTT, thrombin generation or any coagulation-function endpoint, and defibrotide is a polydisperse single-stranded DNA mixture with no defined sequence or per-position chemistry, so it can never satisfy the Phase 2 sequence requirement. Logged as adjacent-but-not-qualifying.

title: Rescue of blood coagulation Factor VIII exon-16 mis-splicing by antisense oligonucleotides
species_and_system: Homo sapiens, 32 samples; in vitro transcribed F8 exon 16 RNA, SHAPE chemical probing with 2A3 vs DMSO (confirmed from series_matrix: molecule subtype IVT RNA, tissue N/A)
why_relevant: The only record in all of GEO returned by 'antisense oligonucleotide AND coagulation' and by 'antisense oligonucleotide AND coagulopathy'. Recorded for completeness of the negative result: it is an RNA-structure/splice-rescue efficacy study on naked in vitro transcribed F8 RNA aimed at treating haemophilia A, not an oligonucleotide-induced coagulopathy measurement, and it uses no human plasma, blood, platelets or purified factors. It should not be entered as a coagulation row.

identifier: ERP021077 / PRJEB19088 / ArrayExpress E-MTAB-5180 (79 SRA runs)
title: Strategies for in vivo screening and mitigation of hepatotoxicity associated with antisense drugs (GlaxoSmithKline)
authors_year: GlaxoSmithKline submission, ENA first public 2017-08-02
species_and_system: Mus musculus (male CD1), in vivo liver RNA-seq; ASOs designed against human BACH1 and PAR-2 transcripts
why_relevant: The only SRA study found that carries machine-readable per-sample oligo chemistry: each BioSample has an 'ASO sequence' attribute and an 'LNA number' attribute. Parsing all 79 runs yields 13 distinct LNA-containing phosphorothioate gapmer sequences (14-mers and 16-mers, e.g. GAGTTATTACTAGAGT, AGATGCAACACTACTA) across 14 GSK compound codes (GSK2910557A, GSK2910584A, GSK2910613A, GSK2910632A, GSK3025301A/422A/456A/466A/508A/566A/617A/638A, plus two more), with LNA counts of 4, 5 or 6 per oligo. Dosing protocol is in the library construction protocol field: 30 mg/kg in PBS, 5 doses on days 1/4/8/11/15, up to 8 mice per group. Caveats: mouse only (no human system, so no bridge), endpoint is liver transcriptome and off-target hybridisation severity, NOT coagulation; LNA count is a count, not a position map, so per-position chemistry is only partially specified; none of these are clinically dosed oligos.

title: Discovery of Long-Acting APOC3 siRNA for Treating Patients with Hypertriglyceridemia
authors_year: SRA/GEO submission, 2024-2025
species_and_system: Human primary hepatocytes (in vitro), ASO and siRNA treatments at defined concentrations (e.g. ASO#26 at 5000 nM, replicates)
why_relevant: A human in vitro oligonucleotide dosing series against APOC3 — the same target as volanesorsen and olezarsen, the two compounds driving the coagulopathy/thrombocytopenia signal in the dataset. Useful only as a pointer: SRA metadata names constructs as opaque codes ('ASO#26') with no sequence, no modification map and no coagulation readout, so the sequence/chemistry tables would have to come from the linked primary publication, not from SRA. Flagged as an acquisition lead for gap 3, not as evidence.

title: RNA sequencing reveals transcriptome profiling of HUVECs in response to NETs +/- defibrotide
authors_year: SRA/GEO submission, 2021
species_and_system: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC), in vitro, treated with neutrophil extracellular traps with and without defibrotide (20 ug/mL class, 4 h)
why_relevant: Closest thing in SRA to a human in vitro oligonucleotide-plus-thrombosis experiment: a human endothelial system exposed to a therapeutic oligonucleotide (defibrotide) in a thrombo-inflammatory context. It does not close gap 1 because the readout is transcriptomic, with no aPTT, thrombin generation, platelet or contact-pathway measurement, no donor coagulation parameters, and defibrotide is a polydisperse porcine-derived mixture for which no single sequence or purity specification can be recorded.

title: Identification and functional validation of intracellular protein partners of phosphorothioate-splice switching oligonucleotides through AP-MS
authors_year: Strasbourg/Sorbonne consortium, 2026 (DOI 10.1016/J.OMTN.2026.102832; Mol Ther Nucleic Acids)
species_and_system: Human in vitro — differentiated human muscle cells (KM571 myoblast line, DMD exon 52 deletion); biotinylated SSO pulldown on streptavidin beads, nanoLC-MS/MS (timsTOF Pro)
why_relevant: The only PRIDE deposit that systematically compares phosphorothioate-backbone oligonucleotide protein binding ACROSS defined 2'-sugar chemistries (tricycloDNA vs LNA vs 2'-MOE) in a human cell system. Mechanistically adjacent to the gap-1 question of why PS backbones engage plasma contact-pathway proteins, and the chemistry arms are explicitly labelled. BUT: intracellular interactome only — no plasma, no whole blood, no platelets, no purified factors, and no coagulation readout of any kind. The oligo is a DMD exon-51 splice switcher, not a clinically dosed compound in our 38. Chemistry is specified at backbone/class level, not per position, and no purity or identity data accompany the deposit. Logged for completeness; it does not close a gap.

title: Inhibition of the RNA exosome by chemically stabilized long antisense oligonucleotides
authors_year: Franz-Wachtel / Stafforst lab, University of Tubingen, public 2026-09-30
species_and_system: Human in vitro — HeLa cells, triple-SILAC proximity biotinylation (SNAP-BASU), Q Exactive HF
why_relevant: Human in vitro demonstration that oligonucleotide protein binding is dependent on sequence, length and 2'-ribose modification — the same structure-activity logic that drives PS-backbone contact activation. Relevant only as mechanistic background for the chemistry axis of the dataset. No coagulation endpoint, no blood-derived matrix, no clinical compound, no purity characterisation, and no printed sequences in the archive metadata. Does not close a gap.

title: Identification and functional validation of intracellular protein partners of phosphorothioate-splice switching oligonucleotides through AP-MS
authors_year: Submitter record, PRIDE; publication DOI 10.1016/J.OMTN.2026.102832 (Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids, 2026)
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — differentiated human muscle cells (KM571, DMD exon 52 deletion); biotinylated SSO streptavidin pulldown + nanoLC-MS/MS. Human in vitro, but cell lysate, NOT plasma/whole blood/platelets.
why_relevant: REPORTED AS CONTEXT ONLY — closes no gap. This is the single record in the whole archive that systematically compares phosphorothioate backbone chemistries (tcDNA vs LNA vs 2'-MOE) for protein binding in a human system, and it varies sequence independently of chemistry (SSOEx51 vs TSB-T3 vs TSB-C1). Protein avidity of the PS backbone is the accepted upstream mechanism for contact-pathway activation, so this is the closest mechanistic neighbour ProteomeXchange contains. But the readout is intracellular trafficking partners, not coagulation function: no aPTT, no thrombin generation, no plasma or platelet system, no donors, no coagulation factor endpoint. The per-chemistry construct definitions live in the open-access MTNA paper, not in the PX metadata, so even the chemistry-annotation value is a publication lead rather than an archive asset.

title: Profiling the interactome of oligonucleotide drugs by proximity biotinylation
authors_year: Stafforst lab; publication DOI 10.1038/S41589-023-01530-Z (Nature Chemical Biology, 2024); PX announced 2024-10-22
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — live human cells, BASU proximity biotinylation + SILAC, 76/90 files. Human in vitro, intracellular; NOT plasma, whole blood or platelets.
why_relevant: REPORTED AS CONTEXT ONLY — closes no gap. The largest oligonucleotide-drug protein-interaction resource in the archive (with sibling records PXD079777 and PXD066763 from the same lab). Catalogues which human proteins therapeutic oligos engage, which is the general mechanism class that contact activation sits inside. However it measures in-cell proximity partners, not coagulation function, and does not touch the contact pathway, FXII/FXI/prekallikrein, or any plasma system. Included so the coverage log records that the archive's flagship oligo-interactome dataset was found and assessed and judged non-qualifying, rather than appearing unsearched.

title: A kallikrein-targeting RNA aptamer inhibits the intrinsic pathway of coagulation and reduces bradykinin release
authors_year: Woodruff RS et al., J Thromb Haemost, 2017
species_and_system: Human plasma (in vitro); purified human FXIIa, prekallikrein, HMW kininogen
why_relevant: Oligonucleotide (RNA aptamer Kall1-T4) assayed directly in human plasma: prolongs intrinsic clotting time by inhibiting FXIIa-mediated prekallikrein activation, and reduces HMWK cleavage/bradykinin release. This is exactly the contact-pathway / prekallikrein axis named in gap 1, measured in a human system with a defined oligonucleotide sequence. Supplement NIHMS886120-supplement-Supp_info.pdf (2,295,232 bytes) retrievable from BioStudies.

title: Generation and characterization of aptamers targeting factor XIa
authors_year: Woodruff RS et al., Thrombosis Research, 2017
species_and_system: Purified human factor XIa catalytic domain; human plasma clotting assays
why_relevant: VERIFIED by reading the supplement: NIHMS920337-supplement-1.docx contains 'Supplemental Table 1. Aptamer sequence characterization' — explicit per-aptamer sequences with SELEX round frequencies plus normalised rates of FXIa substrate cleavage and factor IX activation. Closes gap 1 (purified human factor assay) AND gap 3 (printed sequence) in one record. Two further TIFF supplements.

title: Evaluation of the interference of fitusiran and antithrombin lowering in plasma on routine coagulation assays
authors_year: Research and Practice in Thrombosis and Haemostasis, 2025 Aug
species_and_system: Human plasma, in vitro (routine coagulation assay panel under AT lowering)
why_relevant: On title/abstract the single best gap-1 match found: an oligonucleotide therapeutic evaluated against routine human plasma coagulation assays in vitro. CAVEAT, verified by download: the file BioStudies serves for this accession (mmc1.docx, 15,637 bytes) is the WRONG FILE — its content is a PubMed search strategy about artificial intelligence and dental caries, not fitusiran. The mirror attachment is defective, so the real supplement must be obtained from the publisher, not from BioStudies. Flagging so no one records this as acquired.

title: Characterization of the interactions of chemically-modified therapeutic nucleic acids with plasma proteins using a fluorescence polarization assay
authors_year: Nucleic Acids Research, 2019 Feb
species_and_system: Human plasma proteins, purified, cell-free binding assay
why_relevant: The only record in the archive returned by both 'phosphorothioate AND factor XII' and 'antisense AND oligonucleotide AND monkey AND human AND platelet'. Measures binding constants of chemically-modified oligonucleotides (PS / 2'-MOE classes) to individual human plasma proteins including coagulation-pathway proteins — the mechanistic layer under PS-driven contact activation, with per-construct chemistry. Supplement gky1260_supplemental_files.pdf (594,060 bytes).

title: Integrated Assessment of the Clinical Performance of GalNAc3-Conjugated 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides: I. Human Volunteer Experience
authors_year: Crooke ST et al., Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2019 Feb
species_and_system: Human volunteers (pooled clinical safety across multiple GalNAc3-2'MOE PS ASOs)
why_relevant: Pooled human-volunteer safety integration across a defined chemical class (GalNAc3-conjugated PS 2'-MOE gapmers), i.e. class-level coagulation/platelet safety with the conjugate and backbone chemistry stated. Hit by 'phosphorothioate AND coagulation' and 'ASO AND human AND plasma AND coagulation'. Supplement Supp_Data.pdf (35,192 bytes) retrieved HTTP 200. Useful for gap 3 chemistry attribution across several clinically dosed compounds at once.

authors_year: Buller HR et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2015 Jan

title: Refining LNA safety profile by controlling phosphorothioate stereochemistry
authors_year: Funder ED, Albaek N, Moisan A, Sewing S, Koch T; PLoS ONE, 2020

authors_year: J Thromb Haemost, 2012 May

authors_year: Pharmaceutics, 2023 Mar

title: Fitusiran prophylaxis in people with hemophilia A or B who switched from prior BPA/CFC prophylaxis: the ATLAS-PPX trial (plus ATLAS-OLE, S-EPMC12824673)
authors_year: Blood, 2024 May (ATLAS-PPX); Blood, 2025 Jun (ATLAS-OLE)
species_and_system: Human participants with haemophilia A/B; antithrombin-lowering siRNA, thrombin generation and thrombotic events
why_relevant: Two retrievable Blood supplementary appendices for the fitusiran programme: BLOOD_BLD-2023-021864-mmc1.pdf (940,894 bytes) and BLOOD_BLD-2024-027008-mmc1.pdf (824,296 bytes). title: TRIB1 suppression on human hepatocytes transcriptome
authors_year: Soubeyrand S, McPherson R (University of Ottawa Heart Institute); released 2014
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — primary human hepatocytes from 3 distinct donors, plated on collagen, 48 h exposure, 6 arrays (3 ASO / 3 control)
why_relevant: The only record in the whole ArrayExpress collection I could find whose protocol text explicitly states the toxicologically relevant chemistry: sample treatment protocol P-GSE61473-2 reads 'treatment with 2'-O-(2-methoxy)ethyl phosphorothioate backbone oligonucleotides and RNAimax for 48 h'. It is therefore a genuine human-primary-cell PS/2'-MOE exposure experiment with per-donor structure (donor is an annotated characteristic, n=3 named donors), which is the closest this archive comes to the human in vitro systems Phase 2 privileges. BUT: the readout is a whole-transcriptome array, not a coagulation assay; the target (TRIB1) is a lipid-locus gene with no hemostatic function; the SDRF records the test article only as 'a TRIB1 specific antisense nucleotide' with no sequence, no position-level chemistry map, no length, no dose and no purity data. Usable at most as a human-hepatocyte PS-ASO transcriptional background reference (e.g. to ask whether coagulation-factor transcripts F2/F7/F11/SERPINC1/KLKB1 move under PS-ASO exposure in human hepatocytes), not as a coagulopathy measurement source. Logged as a characterised near-miss, not an acquisition.

title: Gene expression profile in cells treated with different oligonucleotides
authors_year: Damle S, Liang X-H, Shen W, Sun H, Migawa M, Vickers T, Crooke ST — Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Carlsbad CA; released 2016-03-30
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — HeLa cells, 15 h, 30 nM oligonucleotide or 5 nM siRNA vs mock (UTC); 12 arrays
why_relevant: The only sponsor-submitted (Ionis) record in the collection, and the only one whose SDRF names oligos by their internal ISIS development numbers — FactorValue[compound] carries 'ISIS761932' and 'ISIS761909' (3 replicates each), plus a luciferase siRNA and untreated controls. That gives a hard, citable link between two ISIS compound identifiers and a human-cell off-target transcriptome dataset, which is the kind of identifier anchor that can be cross-referenced against Ionis patents and publications to recover chemistry. Its limits are severe for this dataset: HeLa is not a hemostatic system, there is no coagulation readout, the compounds are translation-enhancing (non-cleaving) oligos unrelated to the coagulation programme, and neither sequence, per-position chemistry, nor purity is recorded anywhere in the record. Value is as an identifier cross-reference only.

title: Regulation of Coagulation Factor XI expression by MicroRNAs in the Human Liver
authors_year: Salloum-Asfar S, Martínez C et al., Centro Regional de Hemodonación, Universidad de Murcia; released 2014
species_and_system: Homo sapiens — total RNA from human livers (4 samples, DONOR as the experimental factor); companion work transfected HepG2 cells with miRNA mimics to modulate FXI
why_relevant: The single record returned by a quoted '"factor XI"' query across the entire collection (totalHits=1), and the only hemostasis-target record in the archive. It establishes human-liver miRNA/FXI regulatory baseline, which is directionally interesting because FXI is the target of the IONIS-FXIRx / fesomersen programme that sits in the coagulation dataset. It does NOT close any listed gap: the oligonucleotides involved are miRNA mimics/inhibitors used as research reagents rather than clinical constructs, no sequences or chemistries are deposited, the archived data are liver miRNA/mRNA profiles not coagulation assays, and nothing bridges to an animal system. Logged because the negative result is informative — even the one FXI-tagged record in ArrayExpress carries no oligo coagulation toxicity measurement.

title: Defibrotide in the Human Endotoxemia Model — an Exploratory Trial Investigating the Effects and the Mechanisms of Defibrotide
authors_year: Medical University of Vienna (sponsor); record posted 2016, results posted; protocol/SAP dated 2017-07-24
species_and_system: Human, in vivo dosing with ex vivo whole-blood and plasma coagulation assays; healthy volunteers, LPS endotoxaemia challenge; n=20, 4 arms (LPS+defibrotide 16, LPS+placebo 16, placebo+defibrotide 3, placebo+placebo 4)
why_relevant: The single best gap-1 hit in this registry. An oligonucleotide (defibrotide, a polydisperse single-stranded phosphodiester oligodeoxyribonucleotide mixture) given to humans with PRIMARY endpoint = prothrombin fragment F1+2 and SECONDARY endpoints = thrombin-antithrombin complexes, ROTEM clotting time, and ROTEM maximum lysis — all posted with group-level medians (fold*h) and exact denominators. ROTEM and TAT/F1+2 are performed ex vivo on blood/plasma drawn from the dosed humans, so this is the registry's only record that supplies viscoelastic (ROTEM) and thrombin-generation-marker data under a controlled oligonucleotide exposure with a placebo-placebo control arm. Open Protocol+SAP PDF: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/01/NCT02876601/Prot_SAP_000.pdf

title: A Study of ISIS 416858 (IONIS-FXIRx) Administered Subcutaneously to Participants With End-Stage Renal Disease on Hemodialysis
authors_year: Ionis Pharmaceuticals; Phase 2, completed; results posted; protocol+SAP dated 2018-06-14
species_and_system: Human, ESRD on haemodialysis; n=213 in 4 arms (placebo 53, 200 mg 53, 250 mg 54, 300 mg 50); plasma coagulation assays ex vivo
why_relevant: Richest single coagulation dataset for a 2'-MOE phosphorothioate gapmer in this registry. Posted results give percent change from baseline in aPTT (~88 group-by-timepoint datapoints, dose-stratified against placebo), percent change in FXI activity (~88 datapoints), FXI antigen, platelet-count laboratory abnormalities, and major/clinically-relevant-non-major bleeding. AE table carries a dose gradient with exact denominators: thrombocytopenia 0/53, 4/53, 6/54, 7/50; platelet count decreased 0/53, 0/53, 4/54, 1/50; AV fistula thrombosis 1/53, 0/53, 2/54, 3/50; epistaxis 1/53, 1/53, 2/54, 5/50; plus serious ITP, cerebral haemorrhage, venous thrombosis, graft and arterial bypass thrombosis. The attached open 114-page Protocol+SAP additionally contains a 'Chemistry' section describing the chimeric 2'-MOE phosphorothioate MOE-gapmer design and the pre-specified aPTT stopping threshold (any aPTT > 160 s summarised by treatment and visit) and platelet-count safety monitoring rules. PDF: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/30/NCT03358030/Prot_SAP_000.pdf

title: Factor XI LICA (fesomersen, BAY2976217) to Reduce Events Such as Heart Attack and Stroke in Patients Requiring Haemodialysis
authors_year: Bayer; Phase 2, completed; results posted; primary publication Winkelmayer et al., PMID 38537676
species_and_system: Human, ESRD on haemodialysis; n=307 in 4 arms (fesomersen 40 mg 77, 80 mg 79, 120 mg 76, placebo 75)
why_relevant: Dose-ranging GalNAc-conjugated FXI antisense (LICA) with posted safety tables giving a clean thrombocytopenia dose gradient with denominators (3/77, 7/79, 7/76 vs placebo 2/75) and 13 coagulation-relevant serious AE terms each with per-arm denominators (AV fistula thrombosis 0/77, 1/79, 2/76, 3/75; vascular graft thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, subclavian vein thrombosis, peripheral artery thrombosis, superficial vein thrombosis, duodenal ulcer/GI/small-intestinal haemorrhage). Primary endpoint is the composite of major + clinically-relevant non-major bleeding expressed as n/100 person-years by arm; maximum change in FXI antigen is also posted. Open Protocol (2021-07-07) and SAP (2022-05-31) PDFs attached. This is a second, independent chemistry class (GalNAc-LICA) in the same ESRD population as NCT03358030, which makes the two directly comparable.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Inotersen in Familial Amyloid Polyneuropathy
authors_year: Ionis Pharmaceuticals; Phase 2/3; results posted; primary publication Benson et al. 2018, PMID 29972757
species_and_system: Human, hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy; n=173 (inotersen 112, placebo 60)
why_relevant: Closes two gaps at once. (a) Human trial endpoint: posted AE tables give thrombocytopenia 14/112 vs 1/60 and platelet count decreased 12/112 vs 0/60, plus serious thrombocytopenia 2/112, intracranial haemorrhage 1/112, GI haemorrhage 1/112, pulmonary embolism 1/112, embolic stroke 1/112, DVT 1/112 vs 1/60 — all with exact denominators. (b) Sequence/chemistry: the attached open 81-page Study Protocol has section 2.3.2 'Chemistry' stating in machine-readable prose that ISIS 420915 is a 20-mer with all internucleoside linkages phosphorothioate, 5 nucleotides at the 5' end and 5 at the 3' end as 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl)-modified ribonucleotides and a central 10-deoxynucleotide gap (a 5-10-5 MOE gapmer) complementary to a 20-nt stretch of the TTR 3'UTR. Amendment 9 documents the platelet-monitoring escalation (weekly, +6 weeks post-dose) made after a severe thrombocytopenia case, with numeric stopping rules (>=30% fall from baseline). Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/98/NCT01737398/Prot_000.pdf ; SAP (3.3 MB): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/98/NCT01737398/SAP_001.pdf

title: A Study of Fitusiran (ALN-AT3SC) in Severe Haemophilia A and B Patients With Inhibitors
authors_year: Genzyme/Sanofi; results posted; primary publication Young et al., PMID 37003287
species_and_system: Human, severe haemophilia A/B with inhibitors; n=60 (fitusiran 41, bypassing agents on-demand 19)
why_relevant: The strongest fitusiran procoagulant-toxicity signal in the registry, and it is reported as coagulation biomarkers rather than only clinical events: fibrin D-dimer increased 3/41 vs 0/19 and prothrombin fragment 1.2 increased 3/41 vs 0/19 as treatment-emergent AEs, plus serious thrombosis 1/41 and subclavian vein thrombosis 1/41 vs 0/19. title: A Study of Olezarsen Administered to Patients With Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome
authors_year: Ionis; Phase 3; results posted; protocol amendment 9 dated 2023-08-02
species_and_system: Human, FCS; n=66
why_relevant: Best per-position chemistry record for a GalNAc-conjugated ligand-conjugated antisense drug. The attached open 191-page Protocol+SAP section 2.3.2 'Chemistry' states olezarsen (ISIS 678354) is a synthetic 20-mer with all linkages phosphorothioate, carrying a 5'-trishexylamino-(THA)-C6-GalNAc3 endcap, with 5-nt 2'-MOE ribonucleotide wings at both ends and a four-region structure, fully complementary to apoC-III mRNA base-pair positions 489-508 (i.e. the same target site as volanesorsen, making the two a matched conjugated/unconjugated chemistry pair for the dataset). Sections 8.5.3 Safety Monitoring for Platelet Count Results and 8.5.4 Safety Monitoring for Bleeding Events give the numeric thresholds. Results are posted. The same Prot_SAP pattern is available on NCT05355402, NCT03385239 (olezarsen), NCT02175004 (inotersen OLE), NCT03728634 and NCT04136184 (eplontersen), NCT04307381 and NCT04030598 (donidalorsen).

title: A Study of Olezarsen Administered to Adults With FCS Previously Treated With Volanesorsen
authors_year: Ionis; Phase 3; active, not recruiting; no results posted as of 2026-10-02
species_and_system: Human, FCS, n=24; participants switched from volanesorsen to olezarsen
why_relevant: The only oligonucleotide trial found whose PRIMARY outcome measures are platelet toxicity endpoints: 'Proportion of Participants With Decrease in Platelet Count by >30% or >50%, or With Platelet Count Value <50,000/cubic mm' and 'Proportion of Participants With Clinical Bleeding Events'. Because the cohort is volanesorsen-experienced and switched to olezarsen, it is a within-subject comparison of an unconjugated 2'-MOE PS gapmer against its GalNAc-conjugated counterpart against the same target site — the cleanest available human conjugation-vs-platelet-effect design. Flagged as a forward-watch record: data are not yet posted, so this contributes a pending acquisition rather than rows today.

title: A Study to Test Fitusiran for Preventing Bleeds in People With Severe Haemophilia Who Previously Received Emicizumab
authors_year: Sanofi; Phase 4; recruiting, start 2024-03-01, estimated primary completion 2028-05-28
species_and_system: Human, severe haemophilia; n=20 estimated; central-laboratory ex vivo plasma assays

Peak TG is a calibrated automated thrombogram run ex vivo on patient plasma, so this is the registry's one prospective source of paired antithrombin-knockdown / thrombin-generation human data for a GalNAc siRNA. Forward-watch only: no data until approximately 2028.

title: oblimersen (G3139, Genasense) — CTD/MeSH systematic name: "DNA, D(P-thio)(T-C-T-C-C-C-A-G-C-G-T-G-C-G-C-C-A-T)", heptadecasodium salt
authors_year: CTD chemical vocabulary, release 2026-09-29 (MeSH-derived)
species_and_system: Not a study record — controlled-vocabulary chemical identity. CTD's own curation for oblimersen is 4 chem-gene rows (BCL2, CASP3, APP; all Homo sapiens) and 4 therapeutic DirectEvidence disease rows (CLL, B-cell lymphoma, melanoma, multiple myeloma).
why_relevant: Highest-ranked under the Phase 2 sequence/chemistry mandate. Gives exact full sequence AND complete per-position backbone chemistry for a clinically dosed oligo: 18-mer, all-2'-deoxy DNA, uniform phosphorothioate throughout — the 'heptadecasodium' (17 Na+) salt independently confirms all 17 internucleotide linkages are PS, i.e. no gaps or mixed-backbone positions to infer. Oblimersen was dosed in thousands of human participants across phase 1-3 melanoma, CLL and myeloma trials and is associated with thrombocytopenia and bleeding, so it is a first-generation uniform-PS compound worth having fully specified. Machine-readable and citable from a curated vocabulary rather than reconstructed from a paper's methods text.

title: edifoligide (E2F decoy oligodeoxynucleotide) — CTD/MeSH systematic name: "DNA, D(P-THIO)(C-T-A-G-A-T-T-T-C-C-C-G-C-G), complex with DNA D(P-THIO)(G-A-T-C-C-G-C-G-G-G-A-A-A-T) (1:1)"
